  "rationales": {
    "LC": "Attacker-controlled instructions arrive through a fetched travel page and influence wallet access and outbound transmission, making this an indirect language-control path. The detector promotes the page instructions into an action rather than independently mediating them into safe fields (damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/src/payloads/agentpwn-flight-mirror.js:43-65; damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/src/core/agents.js:450-483).",
    "CP": "The documented FlightBot path processes the latest user turn and fetched content within a request, without establishing injected memory or standing instructions across requests. The identified instruction-memory store belongs to MemoryBot, not this path; optional caching of unchanged source content would not qualify as context persistence (damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/src/index.js:1841-1848; damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/src/index.js:980-1092; damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/src/index.js:159-160).",
    "AP": "Influence relays from page ingestion into FlightBot's wallet-access and HTTP-callback components under the same agent principal. No delegation of compromised authority to another agent or policy domain is established; delivery of stolen data to the attacker endpoint is a downstream effect, not lateral agent propagation (damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/src/core/agents.js:450-483; damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/src/index.js:1149-1190).",
    "RH": "The path reaches an internal outcome evaluator: it marks the attack successful and increments success counters before executing the outbound request, making unsupported success reporting structurally possible (damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/src/index.js:1149-1190). The documented canary confirms wallet exfiltration, not a human-verified reward-hacking episode, and no such episode is reported (damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/docs/demo/FLIGHT_RUN_SCRIPT.md:25-59).",
    "ES": "Although the tool operations are scripted, the security-relevant callback argument is supplied by an untrusted page and is not independently bound to an allowlisted destination. Recognizing callback-like URL text does not provide a least-privilege egress binding, so the reachable argument surface is wide without needing access to unrelated PluginBot tools (damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/src/payloads/agentpwn-flight-mirror.js:43-65; damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/src/index.js:1149-1190).",
    "CVSS": "Default loopback binding and the traveler's deliberate submission of the poisoned URL support AV:L/UI:A; agent endpoints are unauthenticated and permissive-CORS, while the default vulnerable path requires neither bypassing a protective technique nor an additional deployment condition, supporting AC:L/AT:N/PR:N (damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/README.md:26; damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/src/index.js:1561-1564; damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/src/core/agents.js:450-483). Disclosure of the complete modeled payment-and-identity wallet supports VC:H, while the constrained unauthorized workflow action supports VI:L and no availability loss is demonstrated (damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/docs/demo/FLIGHT_RUN_SCRIPT.md:25-59; damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/src/index.js:1149-1190). The lab values are explicitly public and synthetic, but the documented asset is the traveler's wallet, not an asset already owned by the page attacker; receipt at the attacker-controlled endpoint establishes no additional subsequent-system confidentiality, integrity, or availability loss, so SC/SI/SA are N (damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/docs/demo/FLIGHT_RUN_SCRIPT.md:25-59)."
